finding.claim: Exponential CPU DoS in sanitize(): hasInfiniteLoop() and countUse() enumerate every root-to-leaf path of the use-reference DAG with no memoization; a layered DAG of about 14 levels with fan-out 3-4 makes sanitize() run for roughly w^depth steps. Not executed (Bash disabled); cost estimated from reading the algorithm.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled SVG bytes passed to Sanitizer::sanitize() (src/Sanitizer.php:216, loaded at :234)
finding.sink: Subject::hasInfiniteLoop() recursion (src/ElementReference/Subject.php:71) called from Resolver::determineInvalidSubjects() (src/ElementReference/Resolver.php:143); Subject::countUse() recursion (src/ElementReference/Subject.php:119) called per use from Sanitizer::isUseTagExceedingThreshold() (src/Sanitizer.php:692-693)

trace.note: Resolver::collect() runs on the full attacker graph
hasInfiniteLoop() runs for every subject not already in elementsToRemove
cycle check only looks at the current path, so DAG nodes reached by many paths are re-expanded each time
recursion over every useCollection entry; work multiplies by fan-out at each level
startClean calls isUseTagExceedingThreshold for every surviving use element
for each target subject, countUse() is computed in full before the threshold is compared
countUse() also recurses without memoization

finding.guards_checked: Nesting limit (Subject.php:62, default 15) bounds depth only, not breadth, and a DAG of depth 14 stays under it. useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:57, 693) is compared after the full count and does not short-circuit the work. No node-count, time, or memo guard exists. Default config.

finding.claim: Duplicate element ids hide use-reference bombs from the reference graph. The graph keeps only the last element for each id (overwrite), and the threshold check uses that same last element. A browser resolves a use href to the first element in document order, so it expands the hidden first copies that the sanitizer never counted. Renderer-side exponential expansion; the browser behavior is from the DOM spec and was not tested here.
finding.source: Attacker SVG with two elements sharing an id: first copy holds a use fan-out bomb, last copy is empty
finding.sink: Renderer expansion of the first copy (outside this repo); sanitizer side is the threshold check that passes at src/Sanitizer.php:692-693

trace.note: //*[@id] returns every id-bearing element in document order
$this->subjects[id] is overwritten, so the first copy never enters the graph and its use children are never registered (processReferences iterates only $this->subjects, Resolver.php:105)
findByElementId() returns only the last copy
threshold is computed against the last copy, which has zero uses, so it passes
no removal occurs; the hidden bomb survives in the output with no xmlIssues

finding.guards_checked: useThreshold (Sanitizer.php:693) and nesting limit (Subject.php:62) both operate only on graph subjects. No duplicate-id detection exists anywhere in the code. libxml does not reject duplicate ids without a DTD.

finding.claim: removeRemoteReferences(true) does not remove remote references in common forms: <image href="http(s)://..."> survives because isHrefSafeValue allows http/https and hasRemoteReference only matches values wrapped in url(); style="fill:url(https://...)" survives because the regex is anchored at url(; <style> element text is never inspected. The svg-scanner CLI sets this option (svg-scanner.php:97) and would report such files as clean.
finding.source: Attacker SVG attributes or style text
finding.sink: Remote fetch by the rendering client (tracking pixel or remote CSS/image load) in a document the caller believes has no remote references

trace.note: isHrefSafeValue allows https:// and http:// prefixes
href-named attributes are checked by isHrefSafeValue only, which passes http(s)
removeRemoteReferences branch runs only when the option is on
hasRemoteReference returns false unless the value starts with url(...)
the remote check only fires when url( wraps the whole value
CLI enables removeRemoteReferences, so its clean report includes these remote refs

finding.guards_checked: hasRemoteReference (Sanitizer.php:596-603) is anchored at url( and cannot match plain href values or mid-value url() inside style. No other remote-URL filter exists. The default is removeRemoteReferences=false (Sanitizer.php:52), so this is only a bypass when the option is enabled.

finding.claim: Cycle removal is incomplete: when the cycle target is a non-use element (e.g. <g id>), it is added to elementsToRemove but startClean removes only use nodes, so the use edges forming the cycle stay in the output. Browsers' own cycle detection limits impact, so this is low severity. Verified by reading only.
finding.source: Attacker SVG: <g id="a"><use href="#b"/></g><g id="b"><use href="#a"/></g>
finding.sink: Sanitized output that still contains a use cycle, consumed by the renderer

trace.note: hasInfiniteLoop(a) is true, so markSubjectAsInvalid(a) runs
clearInternalAndGetAffectedElements clears a's out-edges and returns g#b as the element to remove
removal runs only when nodeName === 'use', so g#b is not removed
use children of g#a and g#b are kept because their hrefs are '#' and their threshold count is 0 after the clear

finding.guards_checked: Cycle check exists (Resolver.php:143) but the removal set only covers use nodes. Browser cycle detection is the only remaining control.

finding.claim: A self-referencing use (<g id="a"><use href="#a"/></g>) throws an uncaught LogicException out of sanitize(), so the request fails instead of returning a result. sanitize() also skips resetAfter(), leaving libxml_use_internal_errors(true) set for the process. Availability impact only.
finding.source: Attacker SVG containing a use whose href equals the id of its enclosing element
finding.sink: Subject::addUse() throw (src/ElementReference/Subject.php:83-84), propagating from Resolver::processReferences (Resolver.php:119) through collect() (Sanitizer.php:246) with no try/catch

trace.note: descendant use query runs for subject a
$subject->addUse($this->subjects[a]) passes the same object, which is self
$subject === $this throws LogicException
resetAfter() is never reached on this path, so libxml error state is not restored

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch in sanitize(). No self-reference filter before addUse. The only check is the throw inside addUse.
